2.6 Exercises

Exercise 2.6.1. Let \(C_0\) and \(C_1\) be categories and consider morphisms \(f_0\colon x_0 \to y_0\) and \(g_0\colon y_0 \to z_0\) in \(C_0\) and morphisms \(f_1\colon x_1 \to y_1\) and \(g_1\colon y_1 \to z_1\) in \(C_1\). Show that the composite \((g_0,g_1) \circ (f_0,f_1)\colon (x_0,x_1) \to (z_0,z_1)\) in \(C_0 \times C_1\) is given by \((g_0 \circ f_0, g_1 \circ f_1)\).

Exercise 2.6.2. Let \(f\colon x\to y\) be a morphism in a category \(C\). Prove that the following assertions are equivalent:

  • \(f\) is an isomorphism;
  • for any object \(c\) of \(C\), \(f\) induces an equivalence of the form \[ f\circ -\colon C(c,x)\iso C(c,y)\, ; \]
  • for any object \(c\) of \(C\), \(f\) induces an equivalence of the form \[ -\circ f\colon C(y,c)\iso C(x,c)\, . \]
